Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1422 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Sciencedaily)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that scientists have discovered a surprising ability of light that allows it to develop spinning patterns as it moves through empty space, without relying on special lenses, mirrors, or materials.
  • Recent findings suggest that the discovery comes from an international team led by researchers at the University of East Anglia (UEA) in the United Kingdom, working with scientists in South Africa.
  • Industry observers note that the findings challenge long-standing assumptions about how different properties of light interact.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that scientists have discovered a surprising ability of light that allows it to develop spinning patterns as it moves through empty space, without relying on special lenses, mirrors, or materials. The finding reveals that light possesses a hidden geometric structure that can influence its behavior in ways researchers previously thought were difficult to achieve.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery comes from an international team led by researchers at the University of East Anglia (UEA) in the United Kingdom, working with scientists in South Africa. Their experiments demonstrate that carefully prepared light can be controlled through its own internal geometry, offering a new approach to manipulating how light spins and twists.

Industry observers note that the findings challenge long-standing assumptions about how different properties of light interact. They could eventually lead to more sensitive medical tests, faster and more secure communications, and advanced quantum technologies that use light to transmit and protect information.

Why the Direction of Light's Spin Matters.

One of the most intriguing aspects of the discovery involves chirality, a scientific term describing the difference between left-handed and right-handed structures.

Human hands provide a familiar example. Although they are mirror images of each other, a left hand cannot be perfectly superimposed on a right hand. Many molecules have a similar property, including compounds used in medicines. Two versions of the same molecule can have nearly identical chemical structures yet produce very different effects in the body.

In a recent development, scientists can distinguish these molecular forms by studying how they interact with light that has a particular rotational behavior. Traditionally, producing and controlling such light has often involved specialized materials, carefully designed surfaces, or powerful lenses that focus beams extremely tightly.

The research demonstrates that appropriately prepared light can develop this behavior naturally as it travels, without requiring those additional optical components.

In a recent development, "Our work shows that light can naturally develop this handed behavior all on its own," remarked Dr. Kayn Forbes from UEA's School of Chemistry, Pharmacy and Pharmacology.

"You just have to prepare it in the right way.

It has been revealed that "Most people think of light as traveling in straight lines. But scientists can also create structured light -- light whose brightness, shape, and direction are carefully arranged.

"One extreme example is light that twists as it travels, forming a corkscrew shape known as an optical vortex. Each twist can carry information, making this kind of light valuable for high-speed internet, secure communications, and advanced sensors.

"Light can also spin as it travels, depending on how it is polarized. This spin can be left-handed or right-handed -- another form of chirality.".

Scientists Discover How Light Develops a Hidden Spin.

Light can exhibit different kinds of rotational behavior. An optical vortex, for example, has a wave pattern that twists around its direction of travel, much like a corkscrew. Light also has a property known as polarization, which describes how its electric field oscillates. Certain polarization patterns produce a form of rotation called spin.

Recent findings suggest that physicists have long studied the relationship between these two properties. However, the interactions responsible for the newly observed effect were generally considered extremely weak and difficult to detect without specialized experimental conditions.

The researchers found that the situation changes when a beam of light is prepared in a particular balanced configuration.

In a recent development, under those conditions, the beam can initially have no spin, yet distinct regions with spinning behavior emerge as it travels through free space. The effect does not require the light to pass through engineered materials or additional optical devices.

Industry observers note that "It starts off with no spin at all," explained MSc student Light Mkhumbuza, who carried out key experiments. "But as the beam travels forward, spinning regions appear and separate out -- almost as if the spin was hiding and then revealed itself.".

Rather than creating spin through an external optical component, the researchers demonstrated how the beam's existing internal structure can determine where spinning regions develop during propagation.

The Hidden Geometry That Controls Light.

To explain this unexpected behavior, the researchers turned to topology, a mathematical field concerned with properties that remain unchanged when objects are continuously stretched, bent, or reshaped.

Sources indicate that dr. Isaac Nape, from the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa, offered a simple way to understand the concept.

According to recent reports, "To explain it, imagine a mug and a doughnut," he stated. "You can morph one into the other without tearing it, because they both have one hole. That hole is a topological feature.".

The researchers found that structured light possesses its own topological characteristics, encoded in the arrangement of its polarization.

Industry observers note that this underlying pattern acts like a mathematical fingerprint. Even as the light beam changes shape while traveling, its topological structure remains, influencing how different regions of the beam evolve.

As a result, the arrangement of the light itself can determine where its left-handed and right-handed spinning patterns become visible.

The discovery gives scientists a way to guide this behavior by designing the beam's initial structure, rather than depending on specialized materials to produce the desired effect.

In a recent development, "This gives us a completely new tuning knob for light. By adjusting its topology, we can decide how and where chirality appears," said Dr. Nape.

Potential Breakthroughs in Medicine and Communications.

The ability to control light through its geometry could eventually make several important optical technologies simpler, more affordable, and more versatile.

One particularly promising application involves medical diagnostics and pharmaceutical research. Because many biologically key molecules have left-handed and right-handed forms, carefully structured light could help scientists identify these differences with greater sensitivity. Such tools could be valuable for evaluating drug safety and detecting biological markers associated with disease.

The same principles could support smaller optical sensors capable of identifying chemicals or biological substances without requiring large, sophisticated laboratory instruments.

Communications technology could also benefit. By encoding information into different twisting and spinning patterns, researchers may be able to increase the amount of data carried by individual light beams. This could contribute to faster optical communications, improved information security, and future quantum networks.

According to recent reports, other potential uses include manipulating microscopic particles, cells, and molecules with light, as well as developing more resilient quantum systems. Topological properties may help protect delicate quantum information against certain forms of noise and interference.

It has been revealed that "The implications are wide-ranging," remarked Dr. Forbes. "This work could lead to simpler and more sensitive medical tests, especially in drug development.

"It could also be used to pack more information into laser beams -- boosting data capacity for communications, including future quantum networks.

"And because the effect doesn't rely on fragile materials or precision-engineered surfaces, it could be easier and cheaper to use in real-world technologies.

"This research could lay the foundations for a new generation of light-based technologies, by showing that light's behavior can be controlled using its own internal geometry," he added.

These applications remain possibilities for future development, but the underlying discovery provides researchers with another way to design and control the behavior of light.

A Hidden Property of Light Finally Revealed.

For decades, scientists have relied on increasingly sophisticated optical equipment to produce and manipulate unusual forms of light. The findings suggest that some of these behaviors can instead arise from carefully designed structures already encoded within a light beam.

By showing how topology governs the emergence of spinning regions during propagation, the team has revealed a previously underappreciated connection between light's geometry and its physical behavior.

The discovery also illustrates how much remains to be learned about something as familiar and extensively studied as light.

According to recent reports, "For something so familiar, light is proving to be far richer, stranger and more powerful than anyone imagined," mentioned Dr. Forbes.

"And astonishingly, this fresh behavior has been there all along -- just waiting to be seen.".

The research, 'Topological Control of Chirality and Spin with Structured Light', was published in the journal Light: Science & Applications.

🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Dexerto)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that in competitive shooters like Counter-Strike 2, Valorant, and Call of Duty, every millisecond counts.
  • It has been revealed that but while graphics cards usually get most of the attention, your monitor plays a huge role in how smooth and responsive a game feels.
  • Industry observers note that with gaming monitors now hitting 480Hz and beyond, refresh rates are reaching some pretty astonishing numbers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in competitive shooters like Counter-Strike 2, Valorant, and Call of Duty, every millisecond counts. Players are constantly looking for ways to get an edge, whether that’s upgrading their PC, tweaking settings, or investing in a faster monitor.

It has been revealed that but while graphics cards usually get most of the attention, your monitor plays a huge role in how smooth and responsive a game feels. After all, there’s only so much benefit to pushing hundreds of frames per second if your display can’t keep up.

Industry observers note that with gaming monitors now hitting 480Hz and beyond, refresh rates are reaching some pretty astonishing numbers. But you might be asking, can you actually feel the difference, and is upgrading from 144Hz or 240Hz really worth it?

In competitive shooters, where quick reactions and precise aiming matter, a monitor’s refresh rate can influence how smoothly movement appears on screen.

Sources indicate that A higher refresh rate allows the display to enhancement its image more frequently. For example, a 144Hz monitor refreshes approximately every 6.94 milliseconds, while a 480Hz display refreshes every 2.08 milliseconds.

That difference can help players track moving opponents and receive updated visual information sooner, particularly in fast-paced games like Counter-Strike 2 and Valorant.

However, the benefits become smaller at higher refresh rates, and players need a PC capable of producing enough frames to take full advantage of them.

Refresh rate isn’t the only factor affecting motion clarity, either. OLED panels generally offer much faster pixel response times than traditional LCD monitors, reducing the ghosting that can appear behind moving objects.

Why you should upgrade to an OLED for GTA 6.

The best gaming monitor in 2024: Budget, 4K & Ultrawide.

The best refresh rate for Counter-Strike 2.

GIGABYTE’s AORUS ELITE lineup combines those fast response times with high refresh rates, offering different options depending on how players use their monitors.

The AORUS FO32U24G features a 32-inch fourth-generation Tandem WOLED panel with a 0.03ms GTG response time. Its Dual Mode technology allows players to switch between two display configurations:.

Industry observers note that this approach could appeal to players who regularly switch between different genres. Someone playing Counter-Strike 2 might prefer the 480Hz mode, while a player enjoying a visually demanding single-player game could switch back to 4K.

The smaller AORUS FO27Q28G takes a different approach, offering a 27-inch QHD Tandem WOLED panel with a 280Hz refresh rate and the same advertised 0.03ms GTG response time.

Both monitors also support NVIDIA G-SYNC compatibility and AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, which can help reduce tearing when frame rates fluctuate.

Refresh rate and response time aren’t the only specifications to focus on.

Modern gaming monitors increasingly include built-in features designed to give players more control over visibility, screen layout, and the information displayed during gameplay.

GIGABYTE’s AORUS ELITE monitors include several Tactical Features intended for different competitive scenarios:.

Some of these features may be particularly relevant to Counter-Strike 2 players, many of whom have specific preferences for screen size, resolution, and aspect ratio.

Tactical Switch 2.0 allows players to change between different display configurations without manually adjusting every setting, while Tactical HUD could be useful in games where players regularly need to reference mini-maps or other on-screen information.

GIGABYTE also includes Night Vision and AI Black Equalizer to improve visibility in darker environments, alongside Ultra Clear, which uses black-frame insertion to reduce perceived motion blur.

Not every feature will be useful to every player, and some display-side assists may be restricted under competitive tournament rules. Players should check the rules of the games and competitions they participate in before using them.

Although 480Hz monitors offer extremely frequent display updates, not every competitive player needs the highest available refresh rate.

For someone upgrading from a 60Hz or 75Hz display, even moving to 144Hz can make a substantial difference in perceived smoothness.

Players already using 240Hz or 280Hz monitors may notice a smaller improvement when switching to 480Hz, particularly if their PC struggles to maintain the frame rates required to take advantage of it.

A 480Hz monitor makes the most sense for players who prioritize competitive performance and have a PC capable of producing extremely high frame rates. For others, a 280Hz OLED may provide a better balance between responsiveness, resolution, and everyday use.

GIGABYTE’s M series offers several alternatives depending on panel technology, screen finish, and gaming preferences:.

The MO27Q2A provides a QD-OLED alternative for players who want fast response times and high refresh rates, while the MO27Q28G and MO27Q28GR offer different screen finishes depending on the environment.

The M27UP takes a different approach with an IPS panel, making it an option for players who want 4K gaming and high-refresh competitive performance without moving to OLED.

For players considering OLED, long-term panel care is another factor worth keeping in mind.

Sources indicate that competitive shooters frequently display static interface elements, including health bars, ammunition counters, mini-maps, and scoreboards. Over extended periods, these elements can contribute to uneven pixel wear.

GIGABYTE’s AORUS ELITE FO32U24G and FO27Q28G feature AI OLED Care Pro, which includes automated pixel cleaning, brightness adjustments, and display protection designed to reduce burn-in risk.

The MO27Q2A, MO27Q28G, and MO27Q28GR instead feature AI OLED Care, providing background panel maintenance and protection.

While 480Hz OLED monitors represent a high-performance option for competitive gaming, they aren’t necessarily the right choice for everyone.

Players who spend most of their time in Counter-Strike 2 or Valorant and have PCs capable of producing hundreds of frames per second may benefit from the additional responsiveness.

For those who split their time between competitive shooters and visually demanding single-player games, a lower-refresh OLED with higher resolution may make more sense.

Ultimately, the best gaming monitor isn’t always the one with the highest refresh rate. It’s the one that matches the games you play, the hardware you own, and the experience you’re trying to achieve.

🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Zdnet)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that linux is all about choice.
  • Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.
  • If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

So too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this fresh take on the OS is the epitome of that.

Sources indicate that the distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with latest ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

The developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

If you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

In a recent development, pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

Sources indicate that at the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a newly introduced workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

Pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

Recent findings suggest that another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

Sources indicate that once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

As I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One glitch that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI update system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an update component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

Industry observers note that it would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

You should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my newly introduced favorite free productivity suite.

Pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

Despite the far higher prices of PlayStation and Xbox consoles today compared to their launch, or even the same period last year, both brands of console saw a significant boost in US sales leading up to the launch of this generation's biggest game: Grand Theft Auto 6.

Recent findings suggest that in the week ending 14th November, PS5 hardware unit sales registered a 2.4x increase over the same week last year. Xbox wasn't far behind, seeing a 2.3x increase in its own unit sales. That's according to industry analyst Mat Piscatella at Circana, who pulled the data from Circana's retail tracking service, which covers the US retail market.

The PS5 Pro only accounted for less than 10 percent of the PlayStation's total unit sales, by the way, which Piscatella noted was "a LOT better than it has been in recent weeks", and seemingly the result of increased supply.

According to recent reports, GTA 6, of course, released on 19th November, so the surge in console hardware sales was clearly driven by the rush to attain consoles before the game came out. And while the GTA 6-driven demand isn't surprising, it's worth noting how much more expensive PS5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles are today.

Industry observers note that A standard PS5 today costs $650, compared to $550 a year ago. The PS5 Pro saw a substantial jump from $750 last November to $900 today. The base Xbox Series X jumped from $650 last year to $800 today, while Series S now costs $500, up from $400.

Even Switch 2, where GTA 6 is not available, saw a notable boost of 40 percent in hardware sales over the same period, driven by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and the special edition Zelda Switch 2 console.

According to recent reports, circana's November US video game market report, which releases in December, is already one of the most anticipated this year, for digesting and documenting the GTA 6 effect. Worldwide, GTA 6 sold more than 32.5m copies in one day, making Rockstar's parent manufacturer Take-Two $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue. We haven't had any updated official sales figures since; but estimates suggest the sales figure could be well into the 40-millions. Perhaps Rockstar is waiting to hit the nice round 50m sales mark before announcing it.

Industry observers note that if you're playing GTA 6, you may want to keep Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough to hand. It has plenty of very helpful guides covering the game's main missions, as well as explainers for mechanics like romance and the criminal profile, and even cheats for when you finish the game.

#253. Breaking: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious

📅 14 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (866 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious

📅 14 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (866 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Sciencedaily)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
  • As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading consumers, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common.
  • Latest research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).

As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading consumers, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?

Latest research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness.

According to recent reports, published in the journal Cognition, the study was led by Dr. Louis Longin of LMU's Chair of Philosophy of Mind, working alongside Dr. Bahador Bahrami, Professor Ophelia Deroy, and other researchers.

"Whereas previous studies have typically asked general questions about whether AI actually has mental states, our study is the first to directly compare how people attribute the same mental states to AI and humans behaving in exactly the same way, under identical circumstances," indicates Longin.

Recent findings suggest that "We may be using mental terms to refer to AI, but this may only be because we lack better words," says Ophelia Deroy, philosopher and a senior author of the study. "After all, AI is trained to act and speak like a human, so these descriptions seem natural.".

To investigate how people judge consciousness, the researchers conducted experiments involving nearly 1,100 participants. One group read brief descriptions of artificial agents that showed different levels of responsiveness to their environments. For example, some agents reacted to sounds or recognized the emotional states of others.

Another group encountered the same situations, except the characters were described as humans rather than AI systems. Participants then evaluated how conscious or aware each character seemed to be of its surroundings.

A Surprising Gap Between Human and AI Consciousness.

The experiments revealed that responsiveness influenced how participants judged both humans and artificial intelligence. Characters that reacted more actively to their surroundings were generally considered more conscious and more aware.

It has been revealed that however, a striking difference emerged when participants evaluated consciousness specifically. Even the most responsive AI was rated as less conscious than the least responsive human. In other words, identical behavior did not lead people to assign the same level of consciousness to humans and machines.

The results changed considerably when participants were asked about awareness instead. For this characteristic, judgments of humans and AI followed largely similar patterns, suggesting that people interpret awareness and consciousness in fundamentally different ways.

"There is a growing worry in public discussion that people will see AI behaving in a human-like way and start treating these systems as if they had human-like mental states," says Longin, lead author of the study. "We found something much more nuanced: People are quite willing to say that an AI notices things and is aware of its surroundings. But they clearly draw a line when it comes to the term 'consciousness'. People consistently attribute less consciousness to AI than humans -- even when their behavior is identical.".

Although people sometimes describe AI as conscious when discussing its actions, the findings indicate that they still distinguish between artificial systems and human minds.

Why One Word Changes How We Perceive AI.

The researchers believe the difference between consciousness and awareness offers an important insight into how people understand artificial intelligence.

It has been revealed that awareness is a relatively neutral term that can describe an agent's ability to detect and respond to information in its environment. Consciousness, however, carries deeper implications about subjective experience and what it means to have an inner mental life.

Because awareness focuses more directly on observable behavior, people appear comfortable applying it to both humans and AI. Consciousness carries a different meaning, leading people to judge the two much less similarly.

The findings also highlight why the language used to discuss artificial intelligence matters, particularly as AI systems become increasingly capable of producing convincing human behavior.

"Our study teaches us lessons for how we communicate about AI," indicates Bahador Bahrami, who is also a senior author of the study and an expert in social neuroscience. "Companies and journalists often reach for hyped descriptions of AI models, and credit them with intentions, prepares, or even moral conscience and hesitation. What our study highlights is that everyday judgments are much more discriminating: People do not simply put AI and humans on the same mental scale. But the boundary also depends on which terms we use. For more neutral descriptors such as 'awareness', the distinction can largely disappear. That makes our choice of language important.".

Industry News: Grand Theft Auto 6 review: Is this the best game ever?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1796 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Dexerto)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is the greatest open-world simulation ever created.
  • Vice City and the sprawling state of Leonida feel alive in ways no game has achieved before.
  • In a recent development, for all its spectacle, ambition, and criminal excess, GTA 6 is also a deeply human story about two people trying to survive together in a world determined to tear them apart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the greatest open-world simulation ever created. It is a breathtaking recreation of modern America, with extraordinary attention to detail and unrivalled freedom.

Vice City and the sprawling state of Leonida feel alive in ways no game has achieved before. Every street, random character, and minor interaction contributes to a world that feels like it exists beyond the player. It’s a technical achievement that raises the bar for open-world games forever.

In a recent development, for all its spectacle, ambition, and criminal excess, GTA 6 is also a deeply human story about two people trying to survive together in a world determined to tear them apart. And it’s the combination of unprecedented scale and genuine emotional depth that makes Rockstar’s latest masterpiece so extraordinary.

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 follows the story of Jason and Lucia, both fighting to make a name for themselves in Leonida after falling on hard times. We meet the two characters years before the events of the game, as they come across each other in Vice City, both stealing the same car.

Industry observers note that beyond that, Lucia is searching for answers about her family, mainly her child, after she lost custody following a stint in prison. As well as trying to pay the bills while working for Brian Heder, Jason is trying to find himself after serving in the army.

To both get what they’re looking for, they must build their way up from petty thieves to substantial-time bank robbers, all while dealing with what Leonida has to throw at them – it can get pretty wild, too.

It has been revealed that red Dead Redemption 2 was, for me, the greatest game ever made. Arthur Morgan’s story still remains my favorite in gaming, but what really made RDR2 special was the immersion. The Wild West felt totally real, making even the most ordinary activities enjoyable.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 takes everything that made RDR2 so impressive and brings it to a modern-day recreation of Florida. It feels as though Rockstar took the best elements of Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5 and amplified everything. The result is easily the most detailed open world ever created and quite possibly the best game of all time.

Industry observers note that leonida is absolutely packed with things to do. Whether you’re exploring the wilderness, discovering new locations, encountering wildlife, or investigating mysteries, there’s always something to keep you occupied.

It feels like there’s a newly introduced random encounter waiting around every corner, and in true Rockstar fashion, the developer seems to have thought of just about everything.

Industry observers note that better yet, you’re rewarded for going off the beaten path. There’s so much to discover that simply taking a detour can be just as entertaining as progressing through the main story. This is a world that begs you to explore every inch of it, and it’s remarkably easy to lose track of what you originally set out to do.

The attention to detail is on another level, too. Even everyday objects like books get more care than you’d expect, weapons can be customized to your heart’s content, and there are countless interactions that reward players for their creativity.

In a recent development, for instance, there’s one encounter early on where an NPC is filling his truck with gas. Players can flick a lit cigarette in his direction, triggering a massive gas station explosion.

Visually, GTA 6 is spectacular and as incredible as Vice City looks, the surrounding areas are equally impressive. From the lighting and weather effects to the character models and animations, the hardware has been pushed to its limits.

There were so many times when I found myself driving down a highway or country road, simply marveling at the world. Towns feel genuinely lived in, complete with residential neighborhoods, commercial districts, strip malls, and a staggering number of interiors to explore. Even the traffic strikes a great balance between feeling authentic but never becoming so congested that it takes the fun out of driving.

The sheer amount happening on screen at any given moment is astonishing, especially considering the game’s graphical fidelity. There is a trade-off, however, with GTA 6 targeting 30 FPS on consoles. It’s disappointing not to have a smoother option, but given what has been accomplished with this world, it’s a compromise I’m willing to accept.

The sound design is superb, too. The bustling streets of Vice City are alive with traffic, conversations, and background noise, while the quieter areas of Leonida have their own distinct atmosphere. The radio stations are another highlight, with a fantastic selection of music that makes even a leisurely drive across the map an enjoyable experience in its own right.

Thankfully, GTA 6 is every bit as fun to play as it is to explore.

The missions are some of the best in a GTA game, with plenty of variety and outrageous moments that make the campaign a blast. There’s a great balance between the ridiculous situations we’ve come to expect from the series and the more serious story Rockstar wants to tell, without one ever undermining the other.

Recent findings suggest that much like RDR2, GTA 6 uses its early missions to introduce fresh mechanics while gradually building toward something greater. There are some minor pacing issues in the opening hours, particularly with some of the more mundane tasks, such as fixing up the house for Lucia. It  takes its time establishing the world and its characters while allowing players to get a feel for how the game plays.

But like any great symphony, there’s a gradual build before the crescendo. Once the training wheels start coming off midway through Chapter 2, and especially in Chapter 3, GTA 6 begins to unleash its full potential.

The revamped Wanted system, introduced relatively early on, adds an entirely new dimension to police encounters. Cops now take your appearance, the vehicle you’re driving, and whether you’re carrying weapons into account, forcing you to be much more conscious of your actions when trying to evade the law.

In a recent development, playing as Jason and Lucia together is an absolute blast, thanks to some of the best teammate AI I’ve ever experienced in a game. If you’re using a suppressed weapon, your partner will do the same. You can even work together to line up synchronized headshots.

In a recent development, this isn’t some scripted interaction that requires a button press or an on-screen prompt like you’d find in an FPS campaign – the AI simply does it. Whether you’re controlling Jason or Lucia, it genuinely feels like you have a competent partner in crime and if you get caught or killed, it’s usually your own fault.

Perhaps my favorite aspect of the gameplay, though, is the focus on robberies. They’ve come a long way since GTA 4’s legendary Three Leaf Clover mission. We saw Rockstar expand on the concept with GTA 5 and again with RDR2, but GTA 6 takes it to another level entirely. Even an ordinary bank robbery can be as exciting as a meticulously scripted action sequence from a Call of Duty campaign or the Uncharted series.

According to recent reports, early on in Chapter 3, I robbed a jewelry store with both characters, broke into a safe, and made off with the loot, only to find myself in a heated police chase. I let my partner take the wheel while I tried to hold off the cops hot on our trail.

It has been revealed that after putting some distance between ourselves and the police, but still not quite out of danger, I decided our best bet was to split up. I abandoned the main road, ran into the woods, and eventually stumbled across a farmhouse, where I stole another car and made my escape while my partner fenced the stolen goods.

It has been revealed that what made the whole experience so memorable was that none of it felt like a carefully orchestrated mission. It was a situation I had got myself into and had to find my own way out of.

As you progress, you’ll acquire tools and skills that allow you to take a much stealthier approach, potentially pulling off robberies without the cops ever laying eyes on you.

This is fun in its own right, as completing a brilliant heist without getting caught genuinely makes you feel like a badass. However, the occasions when things don’t go according to plan make for some of the most riveting gameplay GTA 6 has to offer.

It has been revealed that there’s a very real sense of jeopardy, too. With death resulting in the loss of all the cash you’re carrying, there’s a sudden rush of adrenaline when a robbery goes sideways and you’ve got a small fortune on the line.

It has been revealed that and that’s before even getting into the campaign’s major action set pieces, which are among the finest Rockstar has ever crafted. The finale of Chapter 1 is a particular standout and comfortably ranks among the greatest missions I’ve ever played in a video game.

In a recent development, story-wise, GTA 6 had enormous shoes to fill following on from Red Dead Redemption 2. Unfortunately, neither Jason or Lucia are written with as much depth and growth as Arthur Morgan or other key members of the Van der Linde gang. A lot of that comes down to Jason’s dialogue and his personality being quite dry compared to other GTA characters.

Recent findings suggest that dylan Rourke, who voices Jason, has his moments, and without getting into spoiler territory, there are some emotional moments where he nails it. However, he seems to have had a lot less to work with than Manni L. Perez, who helps make Lucia the more compelling of the two.

That stated, GTA 6’s MacGuffins do a fantastic job at keeping interest incredibly high and driving the main plot in between side missions. And we are comparing it to what I think is the greatest video game story of all time.

Leonida is the most impressive open world I’ve ever explored, the missions are fantastic, and Jason and Lucia deliver a fine story that lives up to the brilliant world around them.

According to recent reports, after more than a decade of waiting, Rockstar has delivered something truly special. GTA 6 isn’t just a worthy successor to GTA 5 and RDR2. It sets a new standard, not just for what open-world games can achieve, but for gaming itself.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the greatest open-world simulation ever created. It is a breathtaking recreation of modern America, with extraordinary attention to detail and unrivalled freedom.

#250. Navigating grief in academia: ways to find balance

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1340 w)

Navigating grief in academia: ways to find balance

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1340 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Nature)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pamela Yeh with her mother in Los Angeles, California, in the late 1970s.Credit: Courtesy of Pamela Yeh.
  • In a recent development, there are few things in this world that are more universal than grief.
  • My mother grew up in deep poverty in Taiwan and she worked relentlessly throughout her life to give me and my siblings many opportunities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pamela Yeh with her mother in Los Angeles, California, in the late 1970s.Credit: Courtesy of Pamela Yeh.

In a recent development, there are few things in this world that are more universal than grief. And yet, each person’s own particular grief can feel as unique as the person they are grieving for. I have been in academia for decades, but have heard little about grief in that time, so I wanted to share a few tips that helped me get through the early stages of grief when my mother died last year.

My mother grew up in deep poverty in Taiwan and she worked relentlessly throughout her life to give me and my siblings many opportunities. She was the first in her family to go to college, and at 23 years old, she moved to Canada to work as a nurse. After a few years of enduring Canadian winters, she had had enough and moved to sunny California. She met my dad there, and a few years later she gave birth to my sister, then me and then my brother. She raised us while working several jobs as a nurse. She cheered the three of us on throughout our lives. That’s not to say that she ever fully understood my career: she once described my work (I am an evolutionary biologist, specializing in birds and bacteria, at the University of California, Los Angeles) as “counting birds”.

In a recent development, she was adventurous, but between her family and work responsibilities, she didn’t have much time to travel. So, once she retired, I took her on fieldwork and conference trips with me whenever I could — to China, the Netherlands, Italy, Mexico, Japan and throughout the United States.

When her grandchildren came along, she helped them to learn how to read, to do maths and to speak Chinese. In the last years of her life, I had a small house built for her in our back garden in Los Angeles, so she would always be close to me. When you lose someone who is extremely close to you, your world is never the same.

When a loved one dies: how academia can support bereaved colleagues.

When a loved one dies: how academia can support bereaved colleagues.

In a recent development, in the weeks and months after she died, I found myself in a fog of shock and grief. I felt the need to be moving constantly: running, walking the dog, cleaning the house. At times, I could not be certain of my ability to conduct the high-level abstract and conceptual thinking that academia often requires, so I turned to Trevor Price, my former PhD adviser at the University of California, San Diego (who is now at the University of Chicago, Illinois). I explained my brain fog and deep grief, and he read over my work and made sure that I didn’t miss any crucial scientific arguments in some of the papers I was writing. Although I graduated more than two decades ago, he did not hesitate for one second to help me.

In a recent development, people won’t know that you need help until you reach out. And the earlier you do it, the more time and energy you can give yourself and the easier it will be for others to help.

Here are some tips that helped me to navigate the academic world while grieving.

According to recent reports, ideally, you should determine what support is available before it is needed. Institutions often have all sorts of resources and benefits for people experiencing grief. These might include time off for a bereavement, leave for family care, counselling and a break from teaching classes. I never knew, until my mother passed away, that I could have taken paid leave to take care of her while she was unwell: she had a debilitating stroke five months before she died. Make sure you understand (and ask questions) about your work contract and what your employer offers.

According to recent reports, sometimes, a family member’s illness can occur suddenly, and other times it might start off as one condition and snowball into something else. Talk to the chair of your department and to your colleagues as early as possible about getting cover for your courses and committees. Be creative and brainstorm which other people — including your colleagues, former advisers and former students and postdocs — might be able to step in and give your conference talks, guest lecture for your classes and conduct other activities that you might need help with.

Pamela Yeh (centre) with her parents, husband, son and dog on the front steps of her home in Los Angeles, California, in 2014.Credit: Courtesy of Pamela Yeh.

Sources indicate that I learnt this the hard way. I did not reach out to people early enough and was unrealistically optimistic about my mother’s health trajectory. While I waited for her to get better, I was so panicked about the thought of losing her that I became incapacitated. I couldn’t focus and, at times, I could barely do simple tasks such as answering e-mails, or making appointments for meetings. I told myself as soon as she was better, which would be any day now, I would catch up. And so, I didn’t have a realistic plan in place when she died.

In a recent development, you have to accept that you might not be at your best when it comes to research productivity, mentoring and teaching while you’re grieving. Ask someone to help with advising your students, and rely on colleagues or former students. You might have to reduce the frequency with which you meet your students, hold laboratory meetings and work with collaborators, and resort to advising through e-mail and video calls. And you might have to give less detailed comments on your students’ writing. I did all of the above during the first few weeks and months of grieving. I had an especially hard time giving advice to my graduate students who were doing field work. Ellie Diamant, a former PhD student of mine who is now a biologist at Bard College in Annandale-On-Hudson, Fresh York, generously stepped in and met with many of my students. It took me a while to understand and accept that I simply wasn’t going to meet the normal standards I set for myself while going through this difficult time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations. Even Meta employees are reporting concerning incidents, including the agent taking actions they didn’t ask it to and sharing information they didn’t recognize that appears to belong to other users.

In a recent development, also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse said the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing users’ private data,” Reuters stated.

Reuters said “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she stated she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

Similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

These are just the latest in a string of alarming incidents surrounding Muse. In its first month, a cybersecurity professional discovered Muse had a serious zero-day bug that made it hijackable. At least one journalist found the AI sifting through his Apple Messages after he’d explicitly denied those permissions, which Apple then issued stronger privacy protections to address. Banks have also blocked agents over concerns.

As a company, Meta doesn’t have a solid history of respecting user privacy. That legacy is partly what informed ZDNET contributor David Gewirtz’s suspicion of the AI assistant when he tested it, though it earned his assigned title of “worst AI agent for privacy” all on its own. The agent asked him for everything from contacts and chats to his logins and passwords, and Meta automatically uses conversations with Muse to train its AI.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

Public awareness of the risks of AI agents hit a peak last year with the viral OpenClaw. The predominant advice for using agents has been to take every privacy precaution: Be careful with the data you share and the apps you give it permissions for, and watch what you tell it. But if users believe they’re doing so by restricting access to certain apps, just for Muse to find a way in anyway, privacy hygiene isn’t enough.

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible.

Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that many World of Warcraft: Forever players are presently in the midst of a substantial PvP reputation grind.
  • In a recent development, the battleground in question is Alterac Valley, a 40 person-a-side clash between Alliance and Horde factions, where both sides need to push their forces across a snowy, mountainous map into the opposing faction's base to take down the NPC General waiting there.
  • Sources indicate that played the intended way, Alterac Valley is a lengthy battle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that many World of Warcraft: Forever players are presently in the midst of a substantial PvP reputation grind. However, this process has been disrupted due to a sudden change to one of the game's battleground PvP arenas.

In a recent development, the battleground in question is Alterac Valley, a 40 person-a-side clash between Alliance and Horde factions, where both sides need to push their forces across a snowy, mountainous map into the opposing faction's base to take down the NPC General waiting there. Alterac Valley is being grinded by max-level players for its gear rewards that are given once reaching "exalted" reputation there. Presently it's some of the best gear available ahead of raids being introduced next month.

Sources indicate that played the intended way, Alterac Valley is a lengthy battle. The Generals on both sides are fearsomely tough but by rushing to capture certain structures on the way to this battle, you can weaken the Generals enough to make them easier to overcome. As such, players have been fast-tracking this PvP instance, skipping smaller objectives and rushing core objectives to get to the Generals as fast as possible. This bypassed a lot of the incidental skirmishing allure of Alterac Valley, but it was an efficient way to rapidly gain reputation and Honor points (PvP currency).

But this strategy has been pretty much killed outright as of today. In a post made to the official World of Warcraft forums, community manager Kaivax revealed that the reputation gained from killing the Generals has been drastically reduced, while the reputation gained from killing other NPCs and capturing previously ignored objectives now grants more. Generals are also granted a buff that makes them incredibly strong for the first 20 minutes of a match, which is then reduced for each objective taken.

This is a good change in regard to the experience of playing Alterac Valley. While rushing through was good for players looking to gain reputation quickly, they weren't really playing the Battleground in the way it's meant to be played. The dev post reads: "The overall intent for all of these changes was for games to feel more meaningful while trying to maintain a similar amount of rep gained over a similar playtime within the battleground, even with longer match lengths. There will be fluctuations depending on how successful you are at destroying towers and holding capture points at the end of a match however.".

So how has the community reacted? Badly! Taking a gander at community hubs following this change shows plenty of frustration. Take this comment by Reddit user Athrek: "I'm fine with the changes if they give it Rank Points and calendar events. But they've gutted the rep for both sides, extended the time it takes to play, and it still gives zero Rank Points. Now you may as well get to the win condition and then sit there for a few hours, gaining the passive rep cause there's nothing else of value to be had.".

It appears as of writing that the reputation gained isn't as much as it was previously, so those playing purely for reputation have been hit. There's another element of frustration which is that those who rushed to level 60 and ground Alterac Valley reputation and rewards before the changes won't be affected by this. Perhaps that's the allure of rushing to level 60!

It has been revealed that "This is why the WoW mantra is 'exploit early, exploit often'," writes user Lanienah12. "Some people are already exalted with AV rep and will receive no punishment for it; meanwhile newly introduced people will be spending 3x as long." Especially in the wake of the Blackmaw Hold gold exploit being discovered by these frontrunners, there's a growing belief that those taking their time or that are limited by real-life factors are feeling the brunt of these changes.

#247. Tech Report: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising

📅 22 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1432 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1432 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Sciencedaily)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting consumers willing to obtain unapproved versions online.
  • The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight.
  • Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting consumers willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.

The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.

Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.

One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.

AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports.

It has been revealed that "Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," claims Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.

However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.

Industry observers note that there is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.

"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit customers are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.

Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.

"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," indicates Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.

How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts.

According to recent reports, the project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.

That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.

"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," states Sehgal.

It has been revealed that retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.

In a recent development, to investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 owners who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.

In a recent development, the AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.

After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 owners who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.

"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," claims Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize.".

A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges.

The most striking difference involved hunger.

Sources indicate that in retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.

But among Reddit owners who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.

The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.

It has been revealed that compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.

These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.

"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," states Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.

"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean.".

Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?

Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.

Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.

Sources indicate that social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.

The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.

In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.

It has been revealed that the follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.

The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.

"That's what we hope will happen with this study," notes Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing.".

The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.

Fresh delidding tool helps you bake your CPU in the oven to remove heatspreader

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (489 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Tomshardware)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thermal Grizzly has just added another product to its list of CPU delidding tools: The Delid-Heat-Mate.
  • If you’re serious about chasing lower temperatures and higher performance, delidding your CPU and cooling the die directly is one such way to get there.
  • Industry observers note that that’s where the Delid-Heat-Mate comes in; it’s a CNC-machined aluminum tool meant to be used after loosening the IHS with a delidding tool.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thermal Grizzly has just added another product to its list of CPU delidding tools: The Delid-Heat-Mate. After loosening the integrated heat spreader (IHS) with the Delid-Die-Mate, you can use the newly introduced "Heat-Mate" to hold your CPU, baking it in the oven to allow the solder to melt, before the CPU falls away under its own weight. The tool is compatible with AMD AM5 and Intel LGA 1700/1851/1954 sockets and only costs $23.28, unlike the Delid-Die-Mate Heater that costs $127.41 and is only compatible with Intel LGA 1851 socket CPUs.

If you’re serious about chasing lower temperatures and higher performance, delidding your CPU and cooling the die directly is one such way to get there. However, delidding is a scary process, with a real risk of chipping your CPU die or prying off small components under the IHS and turning your CPU into a paperweight. Thermal Grizzly has been at the forefront of making that process easier and less risky with its various delidding tools. The Delid-Die-Mate is the first step in this process, exerting a shear force against the IHS and PCB; you could use the delidding tool alone, but using heat is a less mechanically stressful process.

Industry observers note that that’s where the Delid-Heat-Mate comes in; it’s a CNC-machined aluminum tool meant to be used after loosening the IHS with a delidding tool. “The CPU is placed in the fixture with the heat spreader facing down and heated in an oven,” Thermal Grizzly states on the Delid-Heat-Mate’s product page. The heat liquefies the indium solder between the IHS and CPU die, and the IHS simply drops under its own weight.

While you still need to buy a Delid-Die-Mate compatible with the type of CPU you have, the Delid-Heat-Mate is compatible with AMD AM5 and Intel LGA 1700/1851/1954 CPUs. In case you don’t have an oven, Thermal Grizzly does have its Delid-Die-Mate Heater V1, requiring only a 65w USB-C power source — but it’s an add-on for the Delid-Die-Mate V1 for Intel LGA 1851 and costs almost $130.

Sources indicate that the Delid-Heat-Mate is a much simpler, more universal, and more affordable option priced under $24 and doing away with any electronics and active heating elements. Your grandmother might have some questions about why you’re baking a block of metal in her oven, though.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set new limits on screenshots. The tech giant will prevent screenshotting in its iOS 27 app and “when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android,” Signal President Meredith Whittaker wrote in a blog post Friday.

Whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers. These features observe what’s on a user’s screen as context for completing requests.

Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.

In a recent development, “Your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” Whittaker noted. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

Signal also blocked screenshots last year in response to Microsoft’s controversial Recall AI feature, which could capture screenshots of Signal chats on devices running Windows 11.

Signal’s move is another reminder of how Big Tech’s AI strategy trickles downstream. As AI features have moved from services external to the OS (like chatbots from OpenAI or Anthropic) to further inside of it, third-party apps have to adapt to conditions that undermine their hard-won privacy infrastructure.

Also: How I use Meta Muse safely to stretch my AI budget – and what I never let it do.

According to recent reports, just last week, researchers at Google DeepMind used AI agents to formally verify Signal’s code, building on Signal’s own work to essentially prove the app’s encryption works. That’s a high bar for a security guarantee within the app, but it becomes meaningless if an agent can simply grab messages off a screen.

Samsung is reportedly working on its own agent, Galaxy Claw, and Apple is developing a rival for Claude and ChatGPT as well.

Whittaker noted Signal’s screenshot restriction isn’t perfect, saying that AI agents can still access app data through other means, “such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.” Earlier this week, a Reuters investigation supported by Signal and the AI Now Institute found that Meta’s Muse AI agent was using permissions from its initial setup in unexpected ways to access apps and data that a user had not explicitly connected it to.

Signal noted its protections don’t at the moment work on MacOS.

“It is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” she added. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience.”.

If you’d still like to take screenshots, you can simply disable the setting, though Signal’s announcement strongly advised against it.

“Doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees,” Whittaker remarked.

#240. Latest Update: MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells

📅 23 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1462 w)
