💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that an expanse of stars gleams in a rainbow of colors in these NASA Hubble Space Telescope images of the Milky Way.
  • Astronomers study the Milky Way’s galactic bulge because it holds nearly a quarter of the galaxy’s stellar mass, and its proximity allows them to examine the region in greater detail.
  • Hubble views the universe primarily in ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared light, while Roman collects data in near-infrared light and some visible light.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that an expanse of stars gleams in a rainbow of colors in these NASA Hubble Space Telescope images of the Milky Way. The images focus on an area of sky toward the galactic bulge, a densely packed, spherical region of stars that surrounds the center of a galaxy’s disk. These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy.

Astronomers study the Milky Way’s galactic bulge because it holds nearly a quarter of the galaxy’s stellar mass, and its proximity allows them to examine the region in greater detail. Although we can see the glow from these crowded spheres of stars in other galaxies, they are too jam-packed and far away to resolve individual stars. By studying the Milky Way’s galactic bulge, researchers hope to find upcoming planets and better understand how galaxies form, evolve, and interact over billions of years.

Hubble views the universe primarily in ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared light, while Roman collects data in near-infrared light and some visible light. Because researchers wish to compare Hubble’s observations to future Roman observations, Hubble looked at the region in wavelengths that overlap with Roman’s areas of sensitivity, the red end of the visible spectrum and near-infrared wavelengths.

In a recent development, hubble’s high resolution allows its instruments to collect data on the brightness, ages, composition, and motion of stars over time. With this knowledge, astronomers can search for potential exoplanets, determine the location of black holes or dark matter, and better understand our galaxy’s environment and evolution.

It has been revealed that A key component of Roman’s future observations is the search for exoplanets by capturing microlensing events, a type of gravitational lensing that occurs when light from a more distant object is magnified and distorted by the mass of a closer object along the line of sight. The way light from the distant star is distorted and magnified can reveal clues to the nature of the foreground star and any planets it may have. Hubble's observations will help characterize stars in the region before they undergo a lensing event. Months or years in the future, when Roman captures a microlensing event, researchers can compare Hubble data to Roman data of the event, making it easer to interpret. These microlensing events are on a much smaller scale, that of stars and planets, than larger gravitational lenses that occur around galaxies and galaxy clusters.

According to recent reports, over Hubble’s lifetime, it has observed our galaxy’s central bulge many times. These legacy surveys include the WFC3 Galactic Bulge Treasury Program that used Hubble’s Wide Field Camera 3 to study the brightness, precise positions, and motions of stars in this congested part of our galaxy. It also includes the Sagittarius Window Eclipsing Extrasolar Planet Search (SWEEPS) that used Hubble’s Advanced Camera for Surveys to look at 180,000 stars in the bulge of our galaxy. These newly introduced observations come from an observing program (#17776: S. Terry) designed to aid Roman in its search for exoplanets, black holes, neutron stars, and more. The data also adds to Hubble’s continuing legacy of high-precision observations of stars in the galactic bulge.

Claire AndreoliNASA's Goddard Space Flight Center, Greenbelt, MDclaire.andreoli@nasa.gov.

Hubble's most notable scientific discoveries reflect the broad range of research and the breakthroughs it has achieved.

NASA's Hubble and Roman space telescopes will work together to broaden our perspective of the universe.

The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will settle essential questions in the areas of dark energy, exoplanets, and astrophysics.

Industry News: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach

📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Sciencedaily)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The fundamental difference between human intelligence and artificial intelligence may have less to do with computing power than with the chemistry of memory.
  • Recent findings suggest that hearing a familiar song can transport someone back decades.
  • According to recent reports, like the human brain, computers can store and retrieve information.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The fundamental difference between human intelligence and artificial intelligence may have less to do with computing power than with the chemistry of memory. Researchers propose that the brain not only communicates through electrical signals but may also "write" and "read" memories through chemical interactions involving neurons, astrocytes, and the molecules surrounding them. By linking memory to emotion and thought, the theory raises an increasingly relevant question: Can computational power alone give rise to the kind of consciousness experienced by living organisms?

Recent findings suggest that hearing a familiar song can transport someone back decades. A distinctive scent can bring a forgotten person or place to mind, while recalling a terrifying experience can trigger both emotional and physical reactions within moments.

According to recent reports, like the human brain, computers can store and retrieve information. However, the mechanisms underlying biological memory may be fundamentally different.

A new review by Dr. Gerard Marx of MX Biotech Ltd. and Professor Chaim Gilon of the Department of Chemistry at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem explores the physical and chemical mechanisms that could link memory, emotion, and thought.

Sources indicate that in their paper, "Consciousness, Memory and Intelligence: A Mechanistic Perspective," the researchers suggest that understanding memory requires more than studying neurons and their electrical activity. They argue that other brain cells, particularly astrocytes, and the intricate molecular environment surrounding them may also play essential roles.

Building on their previous research into the molecular foundations of memory, Marx and Gilon examine whether the processes responsible for storing and retrieving experiences could also shed light on the origins of intelligence, thought, and consciousness.

The Brain's Hidden Chemical Code for Memory.

Central to the researchers' proposal is a model known as the Tripartite Mechanism of Memory.

According to this theory, memories emerge from interactions between three major components: brain cells, especially astrocytes working alongside neurons; the molecular substances surrounding those cells; and various chemicals, including metal ions, neurotransmitters, and gliotransmitters.

Rather than relying exclusively on electrical communication between neurons, the brain may use chemical processes to encode and retrieve information.

It has been revealed that astrocytes, which are abundant throughout the brain and maintain close interactions with neurons, are particularly notable to this proposed mechanism. Marx and Gilon suggest that groups of astrocytes help process cognitive information through their interactions with neurons and the extracellular environment, the space and molecular material surrounding brain cells.

The newly introduced paper expands this hypothesis to explore the nature of thought itself. If the brain can physically encode an experience as a memory, the process of recovering that information, recognizing it, and interpreting its significance might contribute to the formation of thoughts.

Why Memories Carry Emotional Meaning.

One of the central arguments of the researchers' theory is that biological memories contain more than stored information. They are also closely connected to emotional experiences.

A scent associated with childhood may spark feelings of happiness. Hearing a familiar voice can provide reassurance, while remembering a frightening event may produce an immediate physical response.

According to recent reports, marx and Gilon contend that a physical model of memory must account for these emotional associations. Their proposed mechanism incorporates neurotransmitters and other chemical messengers that may help encode cognitive information alongside its emotional significance.

This potential biochemical connection between memory and emotion provides a starting point for investigating larger questions about how the brain generates thought, intelligence, and conscious experiences.

What Human Consciousness May Have That AI Lacks.

The rapid development of artificial intelligence makes these ideas particularly relevant.

Although computers and brains can both retain and access information, the physical mechanisms behind these abilities may differ considerably. Computer memory is ultimately encoded in electronic hardware. Biological memory, the researchers propose, may instead depend on the intricate cellular and chemical machinery of living brain tissue.

This distinction becomes increasingly significant as AI systems grow more capable of performing tasks traditionally associated with human reasoning and intelligence.

Marx and Gilon challenge the assumption that simply increasing computational power and complexity will eventually produce consciousness comparable to that of a living brain. They argue that electronic systems lack the biological structures and emotional mechanisms found in living organisms.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers are not suggesting that AI cannot develop increasingly advanced intellectual capabilities. Instead, they question whether demonstrating intelligent behavior is equivalent to possessing the biological mechanisms responsible for memory, emotion, and conscious experience.

How Memory May Give Rise to Thought.

Sources indicate that marx and Gilon emphasize that their theory does not solve the enduring mystery of consciousness. They explicitly acknowledge that the nature of conscious life remains poorly understood.

However, their proposed biochemical framework offers a different way to investigate the physical processes that may underlie mental activity. By examining interactions between brain cells and their chemical environment, the Tripartite Mechanism of Memory could provide researchers with another avenue for exploring how the mind works.

While their earlier research focused on how memories might be physically encoded within the brain, their latest work addresses a much broader problem.

Understanding how living brain tissue transforms experience into memory could eventually help explain how memories become thoughts, how conscious experiences arise, and what fundamentally distinguishes biological intelligence from artificial intelligence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

McDonald’s to gamers: We are so hip. Ahead of the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI last week, the fast food giant confirmed that U.S.-based gamers can now place an order on Discord to be delivered by Uber Eats. And to demonstrate just how hip the septuagenarian organization is, the announcement appealed directly to gamers with text speak—it’s littered with derivatives of “u” in lieu of “you.” “McDonald’s is showing up on Discord to make it a little easier to get ur McDelivery order when breaking from ur servers just isn’t an option,” the company said in a press release. Yes, that’s verbatim from the Chicago-based company—the sort of appeal that could well remind some people of the “How do you do, fellow kids?” meme featuring actor Steve Buscemi from an episode of 30 Rock. Surprisingly, the announcement didn’t elicit many jeers from the Reddit crowd of Discord users, where many people drew comparisons to now-defunct collaborations between fast food chains and gaming consoles that similarly let gamers seamlessly order food. Hype around the end of a 13-year wait for a upcoming edition of the popular game surely warranted being a little cringey. The company didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment from Fast Company regarding how popular the new ordering option has been thus far, but The New York Times reported that both DoorDash and Uber Eats experienced double-digit spikes in orders in the hours after the game was released. MCDONALD’S LATEST MOVES Even if it’s only a marketing ploy, the Discord ordering optionality illustrates just how much McDonald’s wants to show up for customers. Earlier this month, company executives revealed looks to introduce new value-oriented meal bundles next year to appeal to cash-strapped customers. And its nearly decade-long collaboration with Uber Eats is nothing to scoff at. Earlier this month, the two companies announced that their nearly decade-long partnership will expand delivery to 14 new markets, adding to its existing 30-country market. In a more buttoned-up press release intended for investors, Mason Smoot, senior vice president of global franchising and delivery, said its home delivery option—dubbed McDelivery—is a $20 billion-plus global business each year. Even though the company has been trying for more than a year to overcome a challenging market with its U.S. customers, it’s been making a wide range of attempts to lure them back—and that’s seemingly resonating with investors. While McDonald’s shares are still down for the year, they’ve surged more than 14% in the past month. During that same period, the broader S&P 500 Index has slumped nearly 8%.

Recent findings suggest that hype around the end of a 13-year wait for a latest edition of the popular game surely warranted being a little cringey. The company didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment from Fast Company regarding how popular the new ordering option has been thus far, but The New York Times reported that both DoorDash and Uber Eats experienced double-digit spikes in orders in the hours after the game was released.

According to recent reports, even if it’s only a marketing ploy, the Discord ordering optionality illustrates just how much McDonald’s wants to show up for customers. Earlier this month, organization executives revealed plans to introduce new value-oriented meal bundles next year to appeal to cash-strapped customers.

And its nearly decade-long collaboration with Uber Eats is nothing to scoff at. Earlier this month, the two companies confirmed that their nearly decade-long partnership will expand delivery to 14 new markets, adding to its existing 30-country market.

In a more buttoned-up press release intended for investors, Mason Smoot, senior vice president of global franchising and delivery, remarked its home delivery option—dubbed McDelivery—is a $20 billion-plus global business each year.

According to recent reports, even though the company has been trying for more than a year to overcome a challenging market with its U.S. customers, it’s been making a wide range of attempts to lure them back—and that’s seemingly resonating with investors.

Recent findings suggest that while McDonald’s shares are still down for the year, they’ve surged more than 14% in the past month. During that same period, the broader S&P 500 Index has slumped nearly 8%.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended. World Buffs are powerful stat-boosting effects granted to players in a particular area for certain events. The most common World Buff players see is Warchief's Blessing on the Horde and the fresh Might of Stormwind for the Alliance, which are granted to all players in Orgrimmar, Stormwind, and their surrounding low-level zones when players on their respective faction turn in a specific high-level quest. Now that players are reaching endgame and turning in the required quest, these buffs are popping off constantly. They grant a whopping 300 hit points, 15% melee haste, and 10 mana regen per five seconds for one hour. At lower levels, those are some serious stats, particularly the 300 HP. Unfortunately, players haven't been able to take full advantage of the buffs, as a bug was causing them to be lost when hitting a loading screen. That meant any time a group stepped into a dungeon or took a boat or zeppelin to a new location, their World Buffs would be removed. That has finally been fixed in the latest update, so players can now enter dungeons with World Buffs to help maximize their damage and health. This should be particularly useful for doing dungeons at a slightly lower level than is intended, as the extra HP and melee haste is definitely noticable. Blizzard clarified in the patch notes that World Buffs will still be removed when entering raids, so players won't be able to stack as many World Buffs as possible before raid night, as was the case in previous versions of classic WoW. Other changes found in the patch notes include a fix for an Uldaman boss that players were exploiting to make fast gold. Another is a fix for "a few spells and abilities" that were causing more weapon-proc effects than intended, likely nerfing the DPS of whatever classes were taking advantage of the bug. You can read the full patch notes below. Blizzard recently outlined in the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast how it wants to get rid of the idea of "best-in-slot gear," as well as how the game's has overhauled old-school WoW's player-vs.-player systems. In other Forever news, the game's launch has seen more than 15 million characters created so far, with the highest weekly player numbers for WoW in 15 years. WoW: Forever November 23 Hotfix Patch Notes Classes Druid The 4-piece Feralheart set for Druids now correctly grants 4 Energy regeneration every 1 second for 5 seconds. Priest Mind Vision should no longer proc effects. Shadow Fixed an issue where Dark Inspiration was not granting the correct amount of %Spirit increase if Mind Flay was used to activate it. Fixed an issue where Chastise was not usable in Shadowform. Warlock Destruction Fixed an issue where Intensity was not working on Incinerate. Warrior Fixed an issue where players could have and use Mortal Strike from their spellbook, even without the Mortal Strike talent. This does not remove it from their spellbook but prevents it from being used without the talent point spent. Dungeons Uldaman The Obsidian Sentinel drops loot as intended. Items The Filcher’s Cowl no longer has a level requirement. Professions Cooking Boiled Clams, Clam Chowder, Goblin Deviled Clams, Giant Clam Scorcho, Undermine Clam Chowder, and Clam Linguine each now offer the correct Well Fed bonuses and have been recategorized in the recipe list under “Stamina Food”. Murloc Fin Soup has had its recovery and Well-Fed amounts increased to the next tier of food, bringing it closer to other food of that level. Engineering Fixed a bug that caused Goblin Engineer’s Renewal Gift and Gnome Engineer’s Renewal Gift to appear as broken, unusable question marks in the inventory. Fixed a bug that prevented “The Mortar: Reloaded” recipe from being learned upon learning the “Goblin Mortar” recipe. Leatherworking Fixed a bug that prevented Pattern: Centaur Hoofwarmers from being learnable. Quests Riverglades - Dunston Willis once again runs near the end of the escort “Dunston Checks Out.” Wetlands - After further study, the quest “For Further Study” now has rewards. Wetlands - The quest “Uncovering the Past” now rewards Ironforge reputation. Wetlands - The quest “Gleaning Our Future” now rewards Ironforge reputation. Races Fixed an issue where Wisp Form could be applied to players while they were alive. Spells Fixed an issue where a few spells and abilities were causing more weapon procs than intended. Fixed an issue where World Buffs would fall off when changing areas. They will still fall off when entering raid instances. Fixed an issue where Fengus’ Ferocity was granting twice as much Spell Power as intended. Fixed an issue where Darkmoon Faire buffs were granting twice as much power as intended.

It has been revealed that U.K.-based fintech Payhawk announced a $280 million Series C funding round Wednesday, led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm, making it one of Europe’s largest Series C rounds this year, as noted by Sifted. The round values the company at $2 billion, bringing its total funding to more than $500 million to date.

Founded in 2018, Payhawk is an enterprise financial management platform that helps companies track and manage expenses and procurement using AI agents. Speaking to FinTech magazine, Payhawk’s co-founder and CEO, Hristo Borisov, noted the company saw “an incredible growth opportunity and room to bring finance teams AI-native products that combine agents, payment infrastructure, and enterprise controls.”.

According to recent reports, payhawk competes with spend management companies Pleo, Moss, and Spendesk, and states it operates in 33 countries. Notably, the company said it still has 70% of the $100 million it raised in 2022, a round that valued the company at $1 billion. This fresh capital will support its global expansion. Other investors in the round include Greenoaks, Lightspeed, and QED.

'Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home' at 40: 'Trek' has never been as joyous or fun as in 'the one with the whales'

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Space)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales".
  • After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief.
  • Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales".

After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp?

Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters.

They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III.

Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories.

Industry observers note that "I wanted to make it accessible to people who don't go to 'Star Trek' movies," Nimoy remarked in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Altman. "I wanted to make it a movie-movie. It starts out like a 'Star Trek' movie and then makes a left turn. It is intentionally very different.".

"The Voyage Home" effectively closes the trilogy that began four years earlier with "The Wrath of Khan". The story picks up three months after Spock's regenerated body is reunited with his katra (spirit), though nobody ever explains why Kirk and the rest of the crew are all still wearing exactly the same clothes. Following the self-destruction of Enterprise over the Genesis Planet, the gang are heading back to Earth to face the music for a lengthy rap sheet that includes grand theft starship and insubordination on an epic scale.

But as they voyage home (geddit?) in a reconditioned Klingon Bird-of-Prey nicknamed the Bounty — complete with a cloaking device that will come in very handy when hiding in Golden Gate Park — they learn that an alien probe of unknown origin (one of the coolest "Star Trek" spaceships) is tearing Earth apart looking for humpback whales. With the species extinct since the 21st century, the crew travel back in time via one of the most surreal sequences in "Star Trek" history — Morphing CG heads? What the hell was Nimoy thinking? — in the hope of finding the whales that might just be able to ask politely if the probe might leave us alone.

Industry observers note that screenwriters Steve Meerson and Peter Krikes were assigned to the project early on (working with Nimoy and producer Harve Bennett on the story), and their treatments included a future Earth under threat from a plague and a discarded subplot about Lt. Saavik being pregnant with Spock's child as a result of the pon farr mating ritual. There were also discussions about the Bird-of-Prey decloaking above the Super Bowl, and — most bizarrely of all — a guest-starring role for Eddie Murphy as an astrophysicist who wants to believe in aliens.

Sources indicate that murphy was both a Trekkie and one of the biggest stars on the planet at the time but ultimately decided to make notorious stinker "The Golden Child" instead. "In retrospect, I think I might have been better off doing 'Star Trek IV'," he mentioned later. Paramount had also gotten cold feet about putting the star of the highly lucrative "Beverly Hills Cop" in its highest-profile franchise.

Sources indicate that "Paramount stated, 'We're not going to put out [our] two most valuable assets in one movie – so start over, folks!'" said Nicholas Meyer (h/t The Telegraph), hired to retool the script after Murphy's departure. "That's why I was called at the last minute.".

Recent findings suggest that meyer was already "Star Trek" royalty, having brought the movie series to life as director and uncredited writer of "The Wrath of Khan". Indeed, he's arguably the reason the "odd numbers bad/even numbers good" theory of "Trek" films persisted for so long, having later gone on to co-write and direct "Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country".

According to recent reports, he shared scripting duties with Bennett, with the producer writing the 23rd-century-set bookends of the film, and Meyer handling everything in present-day California. Weirdly, Meyer had prior experience bringing a time traveler to contemporary San Francisco in his 1979 HG Wells/Jack the Ripper adventure "Time After Time".

With the three previous "Star Trek" movies largely studio-based, "The Voyage Home" marked a rare chance for cast and crew to head out on location. The Monterey Bay Aquarium filled in for the Cetacean Institute (slightly implausible home of humpbacks George and Gracie), while the USS Ranger — moored in San Diego and no stranger to Hollywood after "Top Gun" — guest-starred as a nuclear "wessel".

Sources indicate that kirk and co. also headed out onto the streets of San Francisco. Nimoy had toyed with giving them '80s-appropriate disguises, but changed his mind when he realized nobody would bat an eyelid at their 23rd-century civilian attire.

Industry observers note that aside from some second unit work photographing humpbacks off the coast of Hawaii, the whales themselves were mostly animatronics created by Industrial Light & Magic. "One of the reasons we think that ['The Voyage Home'] really didn't win visual-effects awards is people didn't really understand how good [the whales were]," stated executive producer Ralph Winter. "ILM did such a good job on those whales that they went on tour for a year or more around the world to museums because the expertise, the art, and science of what they had done was very good.".

Meyer, meanwhile, fully embraced the opportunity to write a fish-out-of-water comedy, with this seasoned crew of Starfleet veterans struggling to get their heads around the eccentricities of late 20th-century America.

In a recent development, kirk and Spock experiment extensively with "colorful metaphors" — "double dumbass on you!" — while Kirk gets out of paying for dinner by using the convenient excuse that money isn't a thing in the future. Scotty (James Doohan) attempts to talk to a mid-'80s Apple Macintosh via a mouse before he risks screwing with the timeline by 'inventing' transparent aluminum decades early.

And in the film's most famous moment, Spock delivers a Vulcan neck pinch to a punk playing his music very loudly on a public bus, winning extensive applause from his fellow passengers in the process. The nuisance rocker was played by Nimoy's assistant, Kirk Thatcher, who co-wrote the "I Hate You" song that plays on that era-authentic ghetto blaster. He later returned to the role in "Star Trek: Picard", though this time he responded more apologetically to Seven of Nine's request to turn it down.

Industry observers note that kirk is undoubtedly the center of the movie, pulling the strings and getting his first romantic interest since the Original Series — whale expert Dr Gillian Taylor (Catherine Hicks), who eventually accompanies the Enterprisers back to the future. But "The Voyage Home" also gives the supporting bridge crew — all of whom reveal a talent for comedy — more satisfying character beats than they'd ever had before. Walter Koenig's W-heavy pronunciation of "vessels" would later be adopted by Anton Yelchin when he inherited the role in JJ Abrams' "Star Trek".

The crew eventually makes it out of the 20th century alive, with the whales safely secured in a giant fish tank so they can make contact with the probe. Of course, what George and Gracie actually say when they arrive in the future remains a mystery; despite Bennett's insistence that the whale song conversation should be subtitled, he was wisely overruled by Nimoy.

Industry observers note that with Earth saved from death by giant cigar, the Enterprise crew have all their charges revoked, bar one, as Kirk is 'busted' down to Captain. The crew is then gifted the shiny new USS Enterprise-A, freeing them to continue exploring the cosmos on the substantial screen.

Which they did, with Shatner taking advantage of a so-called "favored nations" clause in his contract — which meant Paramount had to match anything offered to Nimoy — to direct the rather less positively received "Star Trek V: The Final Frontier", before Meyer returned for "The Undiscovered Country".

According to recent reports, nimoy delivered on his promise to appeal beyond the traditional fanbase, and his reward for earning "Star Trek"'s biggest ever box office haul — a record "The Voyage Home" would hold until Abrams went Trekkin' in 2009 — was directing smash-hit comedy "Three Men and a Baby" the following year. The film also paved the way for "The Next Generation", as Paramount realized the franchise's massive potential, but decided they wanted to cash in without paying mega-bucks for the legacy cast.

Industry observers note that hardcore fans will often claim they prefer the more serious themes of "The Wrath of Khan", "First Contact" or even "The Motion Picture" to "The Voyage Home", but "Star Trek" has rarely been as joyous or fun as on this madcap jaunt to the 20th century. "The One with the Whales" really is one for the ages.

'Star Trek: The Voyage Home' is available to stream on Paramount+ in the US and the UK.

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor.

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest class of drugs led by Ozempic and Wegovy don’t just have transformative effects on the people who take them – they’re reshaping the lives around them too. Patients prescribed GLP-1s are eating less and drinking less, but those behavioral shifts are trickling down to people in their life who aren’t taking the medications themselves. Nearly one in four U.S. consumers have adjusted the way that they shop, eat, and drink based on knowing other people who take GLP-1s, according to a new survey from market research firm Escalent. The survey homed in on a group that the market research group calls “echo consumers,” which refers to people who don’t take a GLP-1 themselves but are changing their habits based on others in their social circles who do. The survey included data from 315 U.S. and 335 U.K. respondents who haven’t taken a GLP-1 drug but know someone who does and report changes to their own behavior based on those social connections. “Much of the attention surrounding GLP-1 medications has focused on the people taking them, and those living in their households,” Escalent Europe Managing Director Melissa Bane wrote. “… For retailers, food and beverage brands and restaurants, that’s a significant consumer group whose changing habits have gone largely unnoticed.” Among the echo consumers, 42% reported exercising more, 36% mentioned they consume more wellness products, and 27% are drinking less. When eating out, 49% said they are ordering less at restaurants when eating with someone taking a GLP-1, while 21% are opting for alternative activities instead of socializing while eating and drinking. Almost one in five say they have picked different gifts for GLP-1 users they’ve shopped for, and many say they are buying different food and drinks to bring along to social gatherings in light of smaller appetites and friends and family who aren’t drinking as much. Industry-shifting numbers While the new survey only offers a small snapshot of consumer behavior, GLP-1 medications are clearly causing some seismic cultural shifts that we’re only beginning to understand. In the U.S., a massive 11% of the population are currently prescribed GLP-1s and 15% say they have tried them for weight loss before. That huge swath of Americans is already walking, running, and cycling more, buying fewer sweet treats, spending less on groceries, and drinking less alcohol. Habit shifts among GLP-1 users alone already represent a massive amount of change for industries to adapt to across just a few short years. Beyond those consumers, Escalent’s survey suggests that there are 1.7 times as many people shifting their behavior in light of the widespread use of weight management drugs than there are GLP-1 users. If similar numbers play out in future research, that’s an even more massive chunk of the population suddenly eating, drinking, and buying differently than they did prior to the advent of drugs like Ozempic, Wegovy, and Zepbound. “For Echo Consumers, a box of chocolates or a bottle of wine may no longer be the gift of choice, and social occasions could increasingly revolve around activities rather than going out for food and drink,” Bane said, calling the changes a “major shift” that will be even more evident during the holiday season. “Brands, retailers and hospitality businesses will need to find ways to adapt their offerings to reflect changing demand as these habits continue to spread through social networks.”.

The Richat Structure, also known as the “Eye of the Sahara,” is seen from the International Space Station as it orbited above on Nov. 14, 2026. It is an eroded geological dome about 100 million years old created by igneous activity and uplift in the nation of Mauritania. In this type of geologic structure, rocks exposed in the center of the “bullseye” are older than rocks forming the outer rings. This structure measures 45 kilometers (28 miles) across and is made up of igneous and sedimentary rocks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.
  • The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.
  • Sources indicate that song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous tech giant to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.

The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.

Sources indicate that song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous tech giant to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024. The company began as a jewelry wholesale business before evolving into a multi-category, factory-direct sourcing platform.

Retailers and brands often rely on intermediaries, face high minimum order requirements, and experience long sourcing cycles, which tie up capital in inventory before sales trends are clear. Song noticed the growing gap between fast-changing consumer trends and traditional wholesale sourcing models while working as a venture investor at Bessemer Venture Partners, where she mostly focused on cross-border sourcing and meeting numerous startups in the sector. That same gap shaped Everful’s goal to simplify buying directly from factories through an AI-enabled platform.

The B2B sourcing industry is highly competitive. Big Tech giant Alibaba connects international buyers with manufacturers and suppliers, while Faire, a San Francisco-based wholesale tech platform, enables retailers to purchase wholesale inventory directly from brands. According to Everful’s co-founders, its key differentiator is responsibility for the sourcing process, rather than simply facilitating transactions.

“We take care of everything,” Han remarked. “We handle sourcing, order consolidation, quality control, and logistics. That’s something the marketplaces don’t offer.”.

According to recent reports, everful is built for smaller retailers and brands without dedicated sourcing teams, Song said, and it also verifies the factories it works with. While peers also offer services such as quality inspection, logistics, and AI-powered sourcing, Everful aims to integrate these capabilities into a more streamlined purchasing experience, creating an end-to-end process that reduces the work retailers must handle themselves.

Han added that Everful uses AI agents to automate labor-intensive sourcing tasks, including tracking consumer trends, identifying suppliers, coordinating orders across factories, and managing logistics.

Sources indicate that because Everful sources from Chinese factories, ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs bear directly on its business. Song mentioned the co-founders have been thinking about geopolitical concerns since day one of building the organization, and that this has shaped Everful’s strategy from the outset, leveraging her experience at Alibaba and Bessemer Venture Partners.

She mentioned the Trump administration’s suspension of the de minimis exemption, which had allowed eligible shipments valued at $800 or less to enter the U.S. duty-free, as one example of a shift in trade policy.

It has been revealed that song explained such changes could favor a model that combines overseas sourcing with local retail sales. “We’re empowering local retailers and brands,” she said. “Long-term cross-border commerce will be cross-border B2B sourcing plus local selling.”.

Industry observers note that everful aims to use the Series A round to expand its presence in the U.S. and Europe, particularly the U.K., France, and Italy, while investing in AI to automate product customization and other sourcing workflows. It also aims to deepen integrations with e-commerce platforms, building on its Shopify integration as it works toward becoming an end-to-end infrastructure platform for global sourcing.

In a recent development, the startup employs about 70 full-time staff globally, including 45 in research and development. It has also established an AI operations team to connect engineering and business functions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, major League Baseball sued its players’ association in federal court on Wednesday, asking that its contemplated lockout next week be declared legal and trying to head off any attempt by the union to decertify and challenge the work stoppage with an antitrust case. In a 38-page complaint filed in U.S. District Court in Manhattan, MLB and the corporate entities owning its 30 teams sued the Major League Baseball Players Association and the eight players on the union’s executive subcommittee, including record-setting pitcher Tarik Skubal. “MLB brings this action to keep the dispute over the next collective bargaining agreement (‘CBA’) at the bargaining table, where federal law claims it belongs,” the lawsuit says. “MLB has a reasonable and imminent fear that the Union will attempt to use the threat of antitrust liability to derail the collective bargaining process altogether in favor of antitrust litigation.” Baseball’s five-year labor contract expires at 11:59 p.m. Dec. 1 and owners are expected to immediately impose a lockout, which would be the sport’s 10th work stoppage since 1972. Owners have proposed a salary cap for the first time since 1994, when players fought off the proposal with a 7 1/2-month strike that led to the first cancellation of the World Series in 90 years. Owners asked for a declaratory judgment determining a lockout doesn’t violate antitrust laws and doesn’t amount to an unreasonable restraint of trade. They asked for a ruling that the federal courts lack jurisdiction to enjoin a lockout and for an order that the players be defined as a legal class, which if granted could block individual lawsuits. “The lawsuit filed today by MLB is completely frivolous,” the union said in a statement. “We will respond appropriately, but MLB’s decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing.” Among the lawyers representing MLB are former Solicitor General Paul D. Clement and Keker, Van Nest & Peters, which worked on behalf of the union in litigation against government seizure of drug tests. “Today’s filing is a defensive measure simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season,” MLB spokesman Glen Caplin said in a statement. “We believe the union is preparing to follow the playbook its new leadership has used against other major professional sports leagues by pretending to ‘disclaim’ its status as the players’ bargaining process.” Caplin referred decertification as a “nuclear option,” mirroring union head Bruce Meyer’s description of the salary cap proposal as a “nuclear bomb.” —Ronald Blum, AP baseball writer.

Soldering is a skill that every hobbyist should master. It doesn't matter whether you're taking your first steps or you're a seasoned pro, because you're going to need an essential bit of kit: a soldering iron.

According to recent reports, luckily, we've put together a good selection of soldering iron deals that are on sale for Black Friday. This is the perfect chance to grab the bull by the horns and upgrade with an iron that will last you through plenty of hefty projects. We've also got recommendations for solder, as well as kit to keep your workbench safe from fumes and heat.

Check out the full list of suggestions below.

The Fnirsi HS-01 is a great soldering iron for anyone who travels or who needs a soldering iron on the go, as our review makes clear.

It's USB-C with an included power supply, or you can use it with a power bank capable of 65W output. It's good for easy soldering, eliminating the need to search for a DC jack or outlet. The flexibility of both a DC and USB-C jack is nice to have, although with so many USB-C PD power banks on sale now, it's a luxury, not a necessity.

The Fnirsi HS-01 is a great soldering iron and well worth the money for those who solder in workshops or in the field.

This kit comes with the soldering iron, but there's also a 96W power supply, a high-quality USB-C cable, a stand, and a selection of soldering iron tips for precision soldering, along with larger tips for when you need to lay down the heat.

It has been revealed that controlling the Fnirsi HS-01 is all about the buttons, which let you control the temperature, as well as navigate the built-in OLED screen. Set your temperature, and the HS-01 will get up to the target temperature in seconds. It's also designed to let you switch holding positions if you're right or left-handed.

Every serious soldering hobbyist needs a desktop soldering station with hot air rework to take things to the next level. The Yihua 995D+ hot air rework station delivers just that, and it's a solid soldering station that will get the job done.

A great selection of soldering tips, a large LCD screen, clear controls and a bonus hot air rework wand make the Yihua 995D+ the best option for those who solder for a living.

In a recent development, the Yihua 995D+ can reach temperatures of 480 °C (896 °F), which gives more than enough heat to solder and reflow even the heaviest solder joint. This soldering station has excellent thermal properties, letting you start soldering speaker wire with ease.

Industry observers note that the stand is compatible with right and left-handed users, as it's separated from the main station, so you'll have free access to the soldering iron while reducing the number of cables trailing across your workbench. It has three preset channels to let you switch between jobs promptly, and it feels great to handle, thanks to a non-slip coating and flexible silicone cord to stop any melting accidents. You've also got a good number of tips, from precision tips to heavy tips for large projects.

According to recent reports, the hot air gun has a similar cable for protection and is easy to handle. You'll need to select the correct controls before using the central knob to handle temperature and airflow. After that, it's easy to control both.

The Yihua 995D+ is an excellent soldering station for both beginners and pros alike. It gets the job done, looks good, and keeps more cash in your pocket.

According to recent reports, if all you need is a reliable and compact desktop soldering station, then the Yihua 939D+ is a good option. This compact soldering station comes with a temperature range of 392°F to 896°F (200°C to 480°C) and ships with a selection of soldering tips to cover many different use cases, from precision to bulky solder joints.

Industry observers note that A solid and dependable soldering station that reduces the cost by omitting hot air rework functionality. This is a soldering station that I could personally use all day, everyday!

It comes with 75W of power, making it suitable for heavier solders like speaker cables. Use the dial to control your settings and the LED display will enhancement accordingly.

It has been revealed that soldering can be a tricky task to complete, and an extra pair of hands is always welcome. Luckily, you don't need a pair of human hands to get the job done, as this helping hands tool can substitute perfectly.

Soldering veterans will know the less-than-glossy metal armature and magnifying glass combos that are available, but this set of helping hands is a little bit different. It comes as a magnetic base, clips, and posts that help to grip your circuit boards as you solder.

With five alligator clips and six posts designed to hold your PCB firmly to the magnetic base, your hands are free to concentrate on soldering up your next project.

Sources indicate that measuring 11.41 x 7.08 inches (29 x 18 cm), this magnetic helping hands kit is sturdy for holding your PCBs while giving you a choice as to how it holds them. The five flexible alligator clips are used to clamp and hold circuit boards a little nearer to the user. The flexibility of the armatures means that both sides of the PCB can be seen, remaining accessible for soldering either way.

According to recent reports, if you need more rigidity, the six posts are used to clamp to the edge of the board you're soldering, which is useful if you're soldering just one side. This is ideal for a maker with plenty of tasks on his sheet.

It has been revealed that you'll want lead-free solder if you're planning on soldering. It's the gold standard, it's safer, and it avoids the environmental issues that come with traditional leaded solder.

Lead-free solder is the gold standard these days. Any modern electronics will have components soldered using lead-free solder. It's safer than traditional leaded, and avoids the environmental challenges, such as lead leakage during bad disposal. It's the safest option if you're planning on making anything you go on to sell, too.

Lead-free solder is better for the environment, and it means you can build and sell products that are made using it.

This 0.6mm diameter solder has a flux rosin core so it flows neatly around your solder joints.

That said, there's still a case for leaded solder, especially if you're using it for yourself (and you take precautions).

According to recent reports, the solder below is worth considering if you need it. It's a mix of 63% tin to 37% lead, which is a decent mix, and should produce good solder joints.

Lead solder is still great for personal use, and this 0.8mm rosin core 63/38 tin / lead mix will melt great and produce shiny and reliable solder joints.

In a recent development, every maker is going to have a workbench that has seen one or two accidents. If you want to avoid any permanent damage, you'll want to pick up one of these sillicone soldering mats.

This silicone repair mat will keep your workbench free from scratches and soldering iron burns. The included magnetic notches and slots will make sure every screw goes back in at the end.

Industry observers note that silicone soldering mats are an essential buy for a hobbyist. They'll keep the heat from your soldering iron away from the workbench, and often have extra positions to keep screws in one place and to stop magnetics from falling off your bench.

Good for taking apart a laptop, for instance. It'll keep your screws safe, the bench burn-free, and it'll help you from scratching the chassis, too. When you're done, you can just roll it up and put it away.

Lead-free or not, you're going to see fumes when you're soldering. It isn't a great idea to breathe these in, so a fume extractor can help you to improve the air quality around you as you work.

According to recent reports, keep your lungs healthy by removing the flux fumes and solder smoke from the air. This tiltable solder fume extractor works from up to five inches away and pulls the offensive fumes through an activated carbon filter to keep the air fresh. You get extra filters in the box.

In a recent development, extractors work, as you'd expect, by using a fan to suck smoke and fumes from the air, directly into an activated carbon filter, with clean air passing through the back of it. This extractor uses a high-speed fan to do it, keeping high suction from up to five inches away: plenty of space for you to solder in comfort.

Sources indicate that this extractor comes with four rubber feet, so it won't move around, and the locking tilt mechanism helps you point it to the right places as you work. It also has fenders on both sides of the fan to stop any breezes from moving fumes away from the unit, as it keeps you safe.

#103. Industry News: The most dangerous election disinformation campaigns

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1949 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fastcompany ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: The most dangerous election disinformation campaigns

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you scrolled through your feed, and a video clip of a candidate’s speech popped up.
  • Recent findings suggest that you scrolled through your feed, and a video clip of a candidate’s speech popped up.
  • Candidates and their supporters spent a whopping $80 million to make AI-generated ads, as part of what AdImpact projected will be the most expensive election cycle on record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you scrolled through your feed, and a video clip of a candidate’s speech popped up. It doesn’t matter who you planned to vote for, the video struck an emotional—and negative—response. The clip was not AI-generated; the candidate really uttered the words you found upsetting. But the story the video told was fundamentally false. That was the 2026 midterms. Candidates and their supporters spent a whopping $80 million to make AI-generated ads, as part of what AdImpact projected will be the most expensive election cycle on record. This is one attempt to capture eyeballs and sway voters. Another is through foreign interference. In just one example, researchers tracking a Russian influence operation recently found a fake video masquerading as a Mother Jones report that captured over 11 million views. But disinformation is not stopping at deepfakes. Authentic videos that are repurposed and stripped of context represent a new frontier. I am not talking about a mere twisting of words. What we’re seeing is next level. THE NEW LOOK OF DISINFORMATION Think about the recent catastrophic flooding in Nepal and India. Some footage released within hours of the floods, intended to showcase the magnitude of the disaster, turned out to be from entirely different events. The footage was authentic. It just happened to be from a glacial flood in Alaska, a landslide in Japan, or a flood that occurred years before. These videos racked up millions of views. They also caused panic among friends and relatives trying to find information about their missing loved ones, and they potentially hindered rescue efforts by confusing the locations where help was needed. Now, consider the same tactic applied in the political sphere—real speeches and words taken drastically out of context, coming from events that could have happened years earlier. One of the most notable examples involved Michigan’s recently elected Democratic Senator Abdul El-Sayed. In August, he was eviscerated by Republicans for apparently calling for Sharia law to take over in America. Social media went crazy. Was the clip real? Yes, it was from a speech he gave in 2022. But the meaning was quite different when you look at its entirety in context. So different that Politifact gave it a “pants on fire” rating for its meaning being distorted. In Georgia’s hotly contested Senate race, Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff ran an ad of Republican Mike Collins urging Americans to get off Social Security and return to work. But that’s not exactly how it went down. The audio came from a broader conversation about tax policy, government revenue, and workforce participation. Collins was not saying retirees should get back into the workforce and lose their benefits (Politifact rated this one as “mostly false”). In both cases, the recordings were authentic. The misleading impressions came from stripping away the information necessary to understand what was being noted, not from manipulating the original material. You may believe that this is just par for the course in a political campaign, but just because something is common does not make it safe, normal, or acceptable. THE IMPORTANCE OF CONTEXTUAL UNDERSTANDING This tactic is becoming effective for two main reasons. Video is now our most prominent data source. Everything is recorded, so if someone is looking for a soundbite to make someone look bad, there is plenty of material available, if they’re willing to dig for it. The second concern is more technical. Deepfake detectors look for signs of manipulation. Authentic videos pass that test. Determining whether a clip is deliberately misleading requires a new set of inquiries, identifying when and where the video took place, what was happening around it, and what the broader context revealed. Making such determinations traditionally has taken a lot of people a lot of time to dig through archives. Even with the deep war chests candidates possess, they’re not going to devote the human resources needed to debunk every false video, at least not in time for that work to make a dent in the video’s impact. So, campaigns take hits, and candidates can spend considerable time and energy trying to explain past comments and rebuild trust. WHAT’S THE FIX? In 2026, voters and media companies are learning that two things can simultaneously be true: A clip can be legitimate while what it depicts is inaccurate. Voters are overwhelmed with election messages. Expecting them to research every clip they see is highly unlikely. Candidates and their backers count on this. Media companies and social platforms bear a greater responsibility, however. Fact-checking and moderation capabilities are essential to reduce the rapid spread of disinformation. Interestingly, while generative AI can be used to create convincing fakes, a different application of AI can be a powerful tool for identifying misleading content and stopping its spread. As good as AI is getting at generating realistic videos, it’s also getting good at understanding them. Solutions that can read a video and its contextual clues can be indispensable in determining whether an authentic video is being misrepresented online. Imagine an instant army of agent fact-checkers. When AI understands video the way a human does, it recognizes not only what is said and who’s speaking, but what else is on the screen and what the setting looks like. It can also search massive archives to see if that moment has appeared anywhere else. And, at the agent layer, tech can flag suspicious content, assembling supporting evidence and escalating cases to human reviewers in minutes. The technology that helps media companies and platforms find original footage, restore full context, and flag misleading claims will enable a faster response, not just to political ads but any sort of controversial content that might catch fire. Stopping the spread of disinformation is a perpetual problem. Thankfully, we are now building intelligent tools that can help. Jae Lee is CEO and cofounder of TwelveLabs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there's been a massive gap between newly introduced entries in The Witcher series, and for The Witcher 4, developer CD Projekt Red aims to make it the GTA 6 of the series, with a noticeable leap in quality. In its Q3 earnings call, the studio notes it has been inspired by the technological and gameplay advancements Rockstar Games has made with GTA 6--especially when compared to 2013's GTA 5--and hopes players will feel the same way when they jump into The Witcher 4. "First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski (via Eurogamer). "But I do understand the connection here. Having stated that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4--I think so, yes. It's been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4c1rokekgnY When The Witcher 3: The Wild Hunt was first released in 2015, it was hailed for raising the bar for open-world adventure games. Its side-quests were singled out for being narratively dense, full of micro-consequences, and on par with the main campaign missions. In the years since, numerous open-world games have used The Witcher 3 as a blueprint, with notable examples being the Assassin's Creed trilogy of Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla alongside Sony's Horizon Zero Dawn and Ghost of Tsushima. Eleven years later, that bar has been raised again with GTA 6, which offers emergent, player-driven open-world chaos through multiple systems. The world of The Witcher is naturally very different from the consumerism-focused setting of GTA 6, but if The Witcher 4 builds on its predecessor's strengths and adds more nuance to those gameplay mechanics, we could be in for something special. CDPR also said it's trying to make The Witcher 4 more appealing to mainstream audiences, but it hasn't detailed exactly how it prepares to do that. "Our games are different, and they require a certain different approach--we just do things differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of breaking out to the mass market awareness: This is for sure something we consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in the future," Nowakowski said. At the moment, over 500 people are working on The Witcher 4, and CDPR has signed a marketing agreement with PlayStation for the game ahead of its targeted 2028 release. The studio is also chipping away at Cyberpunk 2, but after the launch of GTA 6, the game's creative director joked about canceling it, saying Rockstar's game set a high standard for open-world games.

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

In a 2026 Gartner survey, 87% of customers said companies using generative AI for customer service must provide access to a human agent.

That doesn’t mean customers are against AI. It means businesses need to think carefully about where they use it and where human support still matters.

Every business was built on a dream, and that’s a deeply human thing. When we replace real care with automation in the moments that matter most, we risk chipping away at the very thing that made the business worth building.

In a recent development, so how do you know where AI belongs and which moments need protecting? Start by asking four questions, then test your answers.

Before using AI in any area of your business, ask these four questions:.

Sources indicate that if a behind-the-scenes task is predictable, simple and low-stakes, let AI handle it. If it’s personal, complex or high-stakes, keep a person in the loop.

I recently heard from an AnswerConnect client, Craig Grove, founder of GRT Realty, who learned the hard way where not to put AI. He partnered with an AI answering service, only to realize his leads were hanging up on the robot. After switching to human phone answering, he grew his business from six real estate agents to 70.

It has been revealed that running the four questions tells you where AI could go. Testing tells you whether it’s actually working.

I’ve learned firsthand that even the best ideas benefit from a little testing before they’re rolled out more widely. I’m naturally someone who likes to take action, particularly when I’m confident something has potential. After a few instances where the direction or idea I had in mind wasn’t as great as I thought, I found myself in a place where I’d made mistakes.

Industry observers note that in hindsight, I should have started smaller, talked to more people and got feedback first. I’ve never regretted taking a little extra time to test an idea before jumping in. AI deserves the same approach.

Look at it from two angles: your customers and your team.

Then make testing a habit. Things are constantly changing, including your customers’ expectations. What worked in January can fail by June.

AI is one of the most useful tools business owners have ever had. Used in the right place, it gives your people more time for the work that matters. Used in the wrong place, it erodes the trust your business was built on.

So ask the four questions, test the answers, and keep checking.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Conversations about NASA were the norm around the dinner table during Ashley Knight’s childhood. Her parents worked at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, and discussions about happenings at the agency continued even when they came home from the office.

Recent findings suggest that “I remember a poignant dialogue we had after the space shuttle Challenger disaster,” Knight recalled. “However, we talked just as much about the engaging work my parents were doing inside Goddard’s gates.”.

According to recent reports, her father Lyle Knight was a mechanical engineer, while her mother Julia Knight worked the bulk of her career in human resources. They brought their daughter on center for Take Your Child to Work Day and other events, and over time she became hooked.

In a recent development, “I saw the chambers where spacecraft and instruments were being tested, as well as other facilities used to help further space exploration. Above all, I witnessed the passion and collaborative spirit everyone had at Goddard,” Knight said. “As a child, I found it incredibly fascinating.”.

It all came full circle in late August when, after growing up around NASA and later working several contractor roles for the agency, Knight and a number of her colleagues in the Goddard Office of the Chief Financial Officer were sworn in as federal employees as part of a workforce directive to strengthen the agency’s technical core competencies by bringing mission-critical positions into the civil service.

She began her Goddard career more than two decades ago following graduation from the University of Maryland in nearby College Park. As the job search began after commencement, one organization inevitably stood out, along with one particular mission.

When she came across a contractor job opening at Goddard in support of the Hubble Space Telescope team, Knight jumped at the opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that “Hubble was doing amazing things, and I always admired how they fixed the faulty mirror,” she said, referring to how astronauts and team members corrected an early spherical aberration during the observatory’s first servicing mission. “It was exciting to become involved with such a flagship mission, especially coming right out of college.”.

As a project support analyst, Knight assisted engineers with test aims, data gathering, and hardware procurement for Hubble’s fifth and final shuttle servicing mission.

Following the mission’s completion in 2009 and subsequent end of the Hubble shuttle servicing era, she took on a similar role with the Robotic Refueling Mission in what was then the Satellite Servicing Capabilities Office at Goddard – now known as NASA’s In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing Capabilities Office.

Knight left Goddard momentarily afterward to perform contracting work in support of the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory in Washington. After a phone call, she found her way back as a contractor program analyst in the Goddard Office of the Chief Financial Officer, helping manage labor budgets within programs by avoiding funding lapses and ensuring employees received their paychecks on time.

Following the August ceremony, Knight now carries the title of budget analyst in the Program Analysis Office within the Goddard Office of the Chief Financial Officer, performing many of the same critical duties as a civil servant.

Sources indicate that “While many functions are similar, transitioning into the civil service makes it easier for my colleagues and I to help keep NASA’s missions going from the financial aspect,” remarked Knight. “We have more autonomy to perform certain government-related tasks by being on the government side.”.

The civil service also provides additional training and growth opportunities for such positions.

In a recent development, “Ashley is a great team player. This conversion is a fantastic milestone because it unlocks fresh avenues for her learning and development, and allows us to integrate her into new roles,” noted Linnette Morales, Knight’s supervisor in the Program Analysis Office. “I am thrilled she can now fully access the opportunities on the civil servant side, immensely benefiting both her continued career growth and our organization.”.

In a recent development, the workforce directive, entitled “Restoring NASA’s Core Competencies” and revealed by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman in February, is part of a broader effort to expand the agency’s critical institutional knowledge, increase resources essential for mission success, and maintain U.S. leadership in space exploration.

Sources indicate that “The directive has given our office an opportunity to rebalance positions across the organization and remove limitations that were applied to those who were previously not government employees,” said Lisa Kelleher, Goddard’s chief financial officer. “We are now better able to insource many of our experienced contractor staff, allowing us to build up our in-house core competencies in areas such as budget analysis and accounting, and in turn increase our support for mission success.”.

For Knight, she sees an increasing importance for her organization and hopes to make impactful contributions, especially as work taking place at Goddard helps NASA return a crewed mission to the lunar surface, build a Moon Base, and eventually send humans to Mars.

According to recent reports, “We’re the go-between between NASA Headquarters and Goddard programs, and it’s our job to make it a seamless transition for projects to use money they’ve been given to help get these projects off the ground,” she mentioned. “It’s both vital and exciting with the lunar and Mars endeavors, and I’m proud to play whatever role I can.”.

Decades after first following her parents around center, and now following in their footsteps as a NASA civil servant, Knight is as captivated by Goddard and its people as she was during her early visits.

In a recent development, “Through the years, I’ve noticed everyone remains driven by teamwork and achieving the mission,” she noted. “Everybody wants to succeed together by working toward the same goal, and I’m grateful I can continue to be part of it all.”.

Workers hoard AI knowledge to stay competitive, Anthropic report says

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that AI tools are becoming increasingly ubiquitous, but the best techniques for using them are likely still a secret.
  • AI tools are becoming increasingly ubiquitous, but the best techniques for using them are likely still a secret.
  • This is because workers who develop highly effective AI tricks have no incentive to share them with their colleagues or their bosses, notes a report published Monday by Anthropic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that AI tools are becoming increasingly ubiquitous, but the best techniques for using them are likely still a secret. This is because workers who develop highly effective AI tricks have no incentive to share them with their colleagues or their bosses, notes a report published Monday by Anthropic. Researchers interviewed 66 executives, managers, and employees at 58 of Anthropic’s corporate customers and found that many workers are reluctant to share their best AI tricks, citing reasons ranging from job security to more leisure time. The practice has frustrated managers looking to exploit AI-driven efficiencies. The report quotes one exasperated executive saying, “They don’t want you to know, because they want to use those 10 hours a week to go walk their dog.” AI hoarding is a new form of the age-old workplace phenomenon of knowledge hiding, in which employees deliberately withhold information from their coworkers to retain a competitive edge. Employees in the AI age have even more at stake: their jobs. If the trick they develop is powerful enough, they might render themselves redundant. And even for those whose jobs are secure, revealing a time-saving trick might just mean they are assigned more work. That raises a thorny question for business leaders: How do you incentivize employees to help automate their own jobs? Employers hoping to discourage AI hoarding may need to rethink how they measure and reward productivity. Otherwise, employees might realize that their most valuable professional asset is something they’re better off keeping secret.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PC modders are racing to get GTA 6 playable on PC after the leak of the game's complete Xbox build, but so far it doesn't look too promising. GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive and developer Rockstar Games haven't been sitting idle either, as one of the leads behind the Project Leonida Discord group claimed in now-deleted social media posts that they were stepping away from the mammoth task of getting GTA 6 to run on PC. Project Leonida has also been taken down, but it's not the only group trying to get GTA 6 running outside of PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ble-JJxBBGA None of these groups have succeeded yet, and as Twitter user Chasm detailed online, maybe relying heavily on AI tools isn't the way to go. Dev streams have been full of people leveraging generative AI tools to do something, with several prompts being absolute gems of wishful thinking. Here's a snippet of what people have been throwing at Google's Antigravity, while butchering the English language: Continue working and do apply ever part of the code make no mistakes You need todo one thing at a time not a little bit of everything we need all the game start like the rockstar launch so on that stuff, not in game stuff yet work faster there has to be a faster way to iterate than this Even with an army of enthusiasts throwing prompts and cash at generative AI, a copied version of GTA 6 still seems far out of reach. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick commented in March that the idea of using AI and simply pushing a button to make a hit game was "laughable," and he referenced the music industry, which is grappling with a flood of AI slop to top streaming platforms. "Right now [in music] there are programs that allow you to put out a prompt and get a professionally recorded song spit back out at you. It sounds like a song, but I defy you to listen to it more than once. It's great to send as a greeting card to your partner on their birthday, but that's about it," Zelnick said. Whatever progress is made in the GTA 6 PC port scene, don't expect it to last long before Take-Two's lawyers pounce. The publisher hasn't shied away from protecting its IP in the past, and takedown notices for any future GTA 6-related projects seem likely.
